title: 1.2.29 Describe a Real Object
description: Six variables describing something in the room, printed as a sentence with a template literal. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Pick a real object and declare six variables
steps.instructions: Choose something you can actually see. Declare at least six variables about it: at least two numbers, at least two strings, and at least one boolean. Use descriptive camelCase names.

steps.title: Use two string methods
steps.instructions: Apply at least two different string methods to your text — for example .length, .toUpperCase(), .toLowerCase(), or .includes().

steps.title: Print a description sentence
steps.instructions: Use a template literal with backticks to print one sentence describing the object, embedding your variables with ${...}.

steps.title: Check your types
steps.instructions: Log the typeof at least one number, one string and one boolean to confirm each holds what you intended.

requirements.title: At least six variables declared
requirements.description: Six or more variables declared with let or const

requirements.title: At least two numbers
requirements.description: Two or more variables hold plain numbers

requirements.title: At least two strings
requirements.description: Two or more variables hold text, in quotes or backticks

requirements.title: At least one boolean
requirements.description: A variable holds true or false, either literally or from a comparison

requirements.title: Two different string methods used
requirements.description: Uses two distinct string operations such as .length, .toUpperCase(), .toLowerCase() or .includes()

requirements.title: A template literal embeds a variable
requirements.description: Prints a sentence using backticks with ${...} inside, either directly in console.log or via a variable printed later

requirements.title: typeof is used to check a type
requirements.description: Logs the type of at least one variable
